passages.text: All who are under the yoke of slavery should regard their masters as fully worthy of honor, so that God’s name and our teaching will not be discredited.
passages.sermon:
Some people are slaves under a yoke.
These slaves must consider their own masters worthy of all honor.
They must do this so that people will not dishonor God’s name.
They must do this so that people will not discredit our teaching.
passages.original: Ὅσοι εἰσὶν ὑπὸ ζυγὸν δοῦλοι τοὺς ἰδίους δεσπότας πάσης τιμῆς ἀξίους ἡγείσθωσαν ἵνα μὴ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἡ διδασκαλία βλασφημῆται

passages.text: Those who have believing masters should not show disrespect because they are brothers, but should serve them all the more, since those receiving their good service are beloved believers. Teach and encourage these principles.
passages.sermon:
Some people are slaves.
Some slaves have masters who believe in Christ.
These slaves should not disrespect their masters.
Their masters are their brothers in Christ.
Instead, these slaves should serve their masters even more faithfully.
Their masters are believers.
Their masters are loved by God.
Their masters benefit from the slaves’ good service.
Teach these instructions.
Encourage others to follow them.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ πιστοὺς ἔχοντες δεσπότας μὴ καταφρονείτωσαν ὅτι ἀδελφοί εἰσιν ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον δουλευέτωσαν ὅτι πιστοί εἰσιν καὶ ἀγαπητοὶ οἱ τῆς εὐεργεσίας ἀντιλαμβανόμενοι Ταῦτα δίδασκε καὶ παρακάλει

passages.text: If anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching, he is conceited and understands nothing. Instead, he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and semantics, out of which come envy, strife, abusive talk, evil suspicions, and constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. These men regard godliness as a means of gain.
passages.sermon:
If anyone teaches a different doctrine, he does not agree with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ.
He does not accept the teaching that leads to godliness.
He is proud.
He understands nothing.
He has an unhealthy interest in controversies.
He argues about words.
These things produce envy.
They cause strife.
They lead to abusive talk.
They create evil suspicions.
They result in constant friction.
This friction happens among people with corrupt minds.
These people have lost the truth.
They think godliness is a way to make a profit.
passages.original: Εἴ τις ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖ καὶ μὴ προσέρχεται ὑγιαίνουσιν λόγοις τοῖς τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῇ κατ’ εὐσέβειαν διδασκαλίᾳ τετύφωται μηδὲν ἐπιστάμενος ἀλλὰ νοσῶν περὶ ζητήσεις καὶ λογομαχίας ἐξ ὧν γίνεται φθόνος ἔρις βλασφημίαι ὑπόνοιαι πονηραί διαπαρατριβαὶ διεφθαρμένων ἀνθρώπων τὸν νοῦν καὶ ἀπεστερημένων τῆς ἀληθείας νομιζόντων πορισμὸν εἶναι τὴν εὐσέβειαν

passages.text: Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.
passages.sermon: Godliness is a way of living that honors God.\r\nContentment means being satisfied with what you have.\r\nGodliness with contentment brings great gain.
passages.original: Ἔστιν δὲ πορισμὸς μέγας ἡ εὐσέβεια μετὰ αὐταρκείας

passages.text: For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it.
passages.sermon: We brought nothing into the world.\r\nWe cannot take anything out of the world.\r\n
passages.original: οὐδὲν γὰρ εἰσηνέγκαμεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ὅτι οὐδὲ ἐξενεγκεῖν τι δυνάμεθα

passages.text: But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.
passages.sermon:
Godliness means living to please God.
Contentment means being satisfied with what we have.
If we have food, we have what we need to eat.
If we have clothing, we have what we need to wear.
With food and clothing, we will be content.
We do not need more to be satisfied.
passages.original: ἔχοντες δὲ διατροφὰς καὶ σκεπάσματα τούτοις ἀρκεσθησόμεθα

passages.text: Those who want to be rich, however, fall into temptation and become ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction.
passages.sermon:
Some people want to be rich.
These people fall into temptation.
They become trapped by many desires.
These desires are foolish.
These desires are harmful.
These desires plunge people into ruin.
These desires bring destruction.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ βουλόμενοι πλουτεῖν ἐμπίπτουσιν εἰς πειρασμὸν καὶ παγίδα καὶ ἐπιθυμίας πολλὰς ἀνοήτους καὶ βλαβεράς αἵτινες βυθίζουσιν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους εἰς ὄλεθρον καὶ ἀπώλειαν

passages.text: For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. By craving it, some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows.
passages.sermon:
The love of money causes all kinds of evil.
Some people desire money.
They wander away from the faith.
They bring many sorrows upon themselves.
passages.original: ῥίζα γὰρ πάντων τῶν κακῶν ἐστιν ἡ φιλαργυρία ἧς τινες ὀρεγόμενοι ἀπεπλανήθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως καὶ ἑαυτοὺς περιέπειραν ὀδύναις πολλαῖς

passages.text: But you, O man of God, flee from these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
passages.sermon:
You are a man of God.
Avoid the desire to be rich.
Stay away from temptation and harmful desires.
Pursue righteousness.
Pursue godliness.
Pursue faith.
Pursue love.
Pursue perseverance.
Pursue gentleness.
passages.original: Σὺ δέ ὦ ἄνθρωπε Θεοῦ ταῦτα φεῦγε δίωκε δὲ δικαιοσύνην εὐσέβειαν πίστιν ἀγάπην ὑπομονήν πραϋπαθίαν

passages.text: Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called when you made the good confession before many witnesses.
passages.sermon:
You are a man of God.
You must fight the good fight of faith.
You must take hold of eternal life.
God called you to this eternal life.
You made a good confession of faith.
You spoke this confession before many witnesses.
passages.original: ἀγωνίζου τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα τῆς πίστεως ἐπιλαβοῦ τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς εἰς ἣν ἐκλήθης καὶ ὡμολόγησας τὴν καλὴν ὁμολογίαν ἐνώπιον πολλῶν μαρτύρων

passages.text: I charge you in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who made the good confession in His testimony before Pontius Pilate: Keep this commandment without stain or reproach until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ, which the blessed and only Sovereign One—the King of kings and Lord of lords—will bring about in His own time.
passages.sermon:
God gives life to all things.
Christ Jesus testified before Pontius Pilate.
Christ Jesus made the good confession.
I give you this command in the presence of God and Christ Jesus.
Keep this commandment.
Do not let it have any stain.
Do not let it have any reproach.
Keep it until our Lord Jesus Christ appears.
The blessed and only Sovereign will reveal His appearance.
He is the King of kings.
He is the Lord of lords.
He will bring this about at the proper time.
passages.original: Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζωογονοῦντος τὰ πάντα καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ μαρτυρήσαντος ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου τὴν καλὴν ὁμολογίαν τηρῆσαί σε τὴν ἐντολὴν ἄσπιλον ἀνεπίλημπτον μέχρι τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἣν καιροῖς ἰδίοις δείξει ὁ μακάριος καὶ μόνος Δυνάστης ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ Κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων

passages.text: He alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light. No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him. To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen.
passages.sermon:
God alone is immortal.
God lives in light that no one can approach.
No person has ever seen God.
No person can see God.
Honor belongs to God.
God has eternal power.
Amen.
passages.original: ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον ὃν εἶδεν οὐδεὶς ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ ἰδεῖν δύναται ᾧ τιμὴ καὶ κράτος αἰώνιον ἀμήν

passages.text: Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy.
Paul addresses people who are rich in this present age.
Paul commands Timothy to instruct these rich people.
Do not be proud.
Do not trust in wealth.
Wealth is uncertain.
Trust in God instead.
God gives us everything we need.
God provides all things richly.
God gives these things for us to enjoy.
passages.original: Τοῖς πλουσίοις ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι παράγγελλε μὴ ὑψηλοφρονεῖν μηδὲ ἠλπικέναι ἐπὶ πλούτου ἀδηλότητι ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ Θεῷ τῷ παρέχοντι ἡμῖν πάντα πλουσίως εἰς ἀπόλαυσιν

passages.text: Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and ready to share, treasuring up for themselves a firm foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of that which is truly life.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy.
Paul gives instructions for those who are rich in this present age.
Tell them to do good.
Tell them to be rich in good works.
Tell them to be generous.
Tell them to be ready to share.
By doing these things, they store up a good foundation for the future.
This foundation helps them take hold of what is truly life.
passages.original: ἀγαθοεργεῖν πλουτεῖν ἐν ἔργοις καλοῖς εὐμεταδότους εἶναι κοινωνικούς ἀποθησαυρίζοντας ἑαυτοῖς θεμέλιον καλὸν εἰς τὸ μέλλον ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται τῆς ὄντως ζωῆς

passages.text: O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Avoid irreverent, empty chatter and the opposing arguments of so-called “knowledge,” which some have professed and thus swerved away from the faith. Grace be with you all.
passages.sermon:
Timothy, you are a leader in the church.
God has entrusted you with a sacred responsibility.
Guard what God has given you.
Avoid irreverent and empty talk.
Avoid arguments that claim to be knowledge but are not true.
Some people claim to have this false knowledge.
These people have missed the true faith.
May God’s grace be with you all.
passages.original: Ὦ Τιμόθεε τὴν παραθήκην φύλαξον ἐκτρεπόμενος τὰς βεβήλους κενοφωνίας καὶ ἀντιθέσεις τῆς ψευδωνύμου γνώσεως ἥν τινες ἐπαγγελλόμενοι περὶ τὴν πίστιν ἠστόχησαν Ἡ χάρις μεθ’ ὑμῶν
